case_name: Phanindra Prasad Shukla and Another v State of Madhya Pradesh
respondent:
State of Madhya Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

26 March 1980
Cr.A. No. 71 of 1972
The Judgment was delivered by: PATHAK, J.
1.  This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment dated 10th January, 1972 of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh affirming, in its appellate jurisdiction, the conviction and sentence of the appellants.
2.  The appellants, P. P. Shukla and Uttam Singh, are two of the original five accused. The other accused were acquitted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Bhopal, but the present appellants were convicted under S. 5(1)(c) and S. 5(1)(d), Prevention of Corruption Act read with S. 5(2) of that Act respectively, and u/ss. 109 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code. Shukla was, in addition convicted under S. 477A, Indian Penal Code. Shukla was sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment and Uttam Singh to one year's rigorous imprisonment on each count, the sentences to rung concurrently. Shukla
facts: This appeal by special leave is directed against the judgment dated 10th January, 1972 of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh affirming, in its appellate jurisdiction, the conviction and sentence of the appellants.
The appellants, P. P. Shukla and Uttam Singh, are two of the original five accused.
A sum of Rupees 2,50,000/- was placed at the disposal of the Agriculture Department Government of Madhya Pradesh, for the execution of a Contour Bunding Scheme in the Sehore District of the State.
The case of the prosecution was that the appellants along with three other officers of the Agriculture Department entered into a criminal conspiracy to commit misappropriation of Rs. 744-50.

It is pointed out by learned counsel for the appellants that while the evidence adduced by the prosecution attempted to show that there was no supply of boulders at all by Uttam Singh, the Court has found that a part of the stipulated quantity was actually supplied.
The finding, in our opinion, is sufficient to warrant the conviction of the appellants.
Uttam Singh, on whose complaint the prosecution was launched, has no right to complain as the vouchers leading to the payment were attested by his son, Gulab Singh.
In any event, the conviction of the appellants is founded on an overall assessment of the evidence and is not vitiated by the circumstances on which the learned counsel now rests his submission.
Finally, a plea has been addressed to us in regard to the severity of the sentence.
petitioner_arguments: While the evidence adduced by the prosecution attempted to show that there was no supply of boulders at all by Uttam Singh, the Court has found that a part of the stipulated quantity was actually supplied.
The case of the prosecution must be regarded as false and consequently, the conviction and sentence must be quashed.
Uttam Singh, on whose complaint the prosecution was launched, has no right to complain as the vouchers leading to the payment were attested by his son, Gulab Singh.
court_reasoning: The finding, in our opinion, is sufficient to warrant the conviction of the appellants.
It is not a case where the facts on which the allegation rests are so integrally related that if a part of the case is not proved the rest must fail.
In any event, the conviction of the appellants is founded on an overall assessment of the evidence and is not vitiated by the circumstances on which the learned counsel now rests his submission.
holding: The sentence of a year's rigorous imprisonment is substituted for that of two years rigorous imprisonment imposed on Shukla under the different counts.
